Satchel and Crafting tabs: 3 designs

Same language as the Pantry redesign, built with real data, item squares and forms. Heights are phone (390 px) page heights at the same test data. Today: Satchel 5,859 px; Cooking about 6,300 to 15,800 px per list, about 32,000 px if all 85 recipes were listed.

DesignSatchel (phone)Cooking (phone)
1 · Pantry twin5,007 px (type chips cut it to ~600–1,500)3,624 px
2 · Dense grid + drawer2,989 px2,565 px
3 · Shelves (my own take)3,217 px1,507 px

My pick: 3. Shortest on a phone for Cooking, and answers 'what can I do now / what do I gather next' without filtering. Easiest to port: 1, already proven on the Pantry. Other crafting tabs (tools, garden, building, decor) use the same code in all three: no pots, so the strip shows the Tool Shed or 'No building needed', and groups come from what the recipe makes. Each is about 1,000–1,200 px on a phone.

Design 1 · Pantry twin

The shipped Pantry pattern applied as is: category and kind chips, search, compact list, detail panel (sheet on phones). Satchel gets type chips plus Untasted / New / Needs-care chips and Eat / Cook / Open / Read in the detail; Sell and Gift link to the market tabs. Cooking gets a strip with pots, energy and Petals, plus Snack / Meal / Feast chips.

Port: Smallest. Make pantry_view general (about 40 lines of new CSS). Reuses .pantry2 and the existing site.js sheet code unchanged.

Design 2 · Dense grid + drawer

Mini item squares (64 px art, count badge, rarity gem): 4 per row on a phone, 8 on desktop. Sticky search and chips. Cookable recipes get a tick, missing ones a 'short N' flag. Tap a tile for a drawer (bottom sheet on phones).

Port: Medium. New mini-square CSS and a drawer. Same tile for Satchel and recipes.

Design 3 · Shelves (my own take)

Organised by what you can do, not what an item is. Satchel: a Quick bar (one-tap Eat, Open, Read, Mend) above foldable type shelves of compact pills. Cooking: a Shopping list of ingredients for recipes one trip away, then shelves by readiness: Ready, One trip away, Need more, To discover. The pick opens inline with a You have / Still need split.

Port: Medium. Shelf, pill and quick-bar CSS plus about 30 lines of JS. One shelf-and-pill design serves both tabs.
